summary: The note surveys how seafood availability follows natural cycles tied to water temperature, spawning and food sources, and why fishing calendars support sustainability. It tours seasonal catches and regional dishes worldwide, from New England cod to Japanese sanma and Spanish gambas de Palamós. It closes with chefs' perspectives on culinary calendars and notable seafood festivals.
one_line: A global tour of seasonal seafood, fishing calendars, sustainability, regional dishes and seafood festivals tied to natural marine life cycles.
key_facts: Wild salmon migrate to spawning grounds mainly in late summer and autumn, and spawning salmon have richer flavor from increased fat stores, making autumn ideal for harvesting.
The Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) works to ensure seafood comes from sources rigorously assessed for environmental impact and sustainability.
Atlantic cod in New England is a prime catch from January through March, used in chowders and pies.
Red snapper on the Gulf Coast peaks from June through August, served in dishes like snapper Veracruzana.
Tasmanian crab is fished in Australian waters from October to June, late spring through early winter.
European sea bass (branzino) in the Mediterranean is typically caught between May and July, often cooked in a salt crust or grilled.
In the Pacific Northwest, king salmon rules the summer, and Indigenous communities traditionally prepare cedar plank salmon.
Japan's Pacific saury, called sanma, marks autumn and is often salted and grilled; it is rich in omega-3 fatty acids.
Gambas de Palamós, a prized Spanish red shrimp, peak from December to March.
Walleye pike in the Midwest has a spring run, is prevalent in May, and is often breaded and fried with tartar sauce.
San Francisco Bay area Dungeness crab season starts in mid-November, after molting and before reproduction, ensuring a sustainable catch.
The Maine Lobster Festival is usually in August, and the Hawaii Seafood Festival is in mid-September to coincide with ahi tuna season.
The Festa do Marisco in O Grove, Galicia, Spain, is typically held in early October and features mussels, clams and goose barnacles.
Baja California celebrates yellowtail amberjack in January, while the Canadian Maritimes' lobster season begins by midsummer.
